description: Manual cases for validating Perception Ontology V1

cases.title: Factual question about museum hours
cases.purpose: Distinguish a request for information from a request to perform an action

messages.content: What time does the museum close?

evidence.quoted_text: What time does the museum close?

cue_expectations.rationale: The user asks a direct punctuated factual question.
The message asks for information but does not ask Columbina to perform an external action.

information_available: The user wants to know the museum closing time.
information_missing: Which museum the user means is not established.

routing_expectation.rationale: The question form is explicit; any entity resolution can occur downstream.

cases.title: Action request phrased as a question with a missing recipient
cases.purpose: Show that question form and explicit request can co-occur and that missing constraints require a task contract

cue_expectations.rationale: The action request has interrogative grammar and punctuation.
The user directly asks Columbina to send a report.

post_interpretation_expectations.requires_interpretation: Resolve the utterance to the send_report action before applying its parameter contract.
post_interpretation_expectations.rationale: After action resolution, the trusted send_report contract requires a recipient and none is provided.

forbidden_inferences: The user intentionally omitted the recipient.

information_available: The user requests that the report be sent.
The required recipient is missing.
information_missing: The intended recipient.

routing_expectation.rationale: A required task parameter must be supplied before the action can be executed.

ontology_questions: The location and schema of a task-specific contract are not defined. Suggested change: define the trusted runtime task_contract shape and parameter-presence semantics.

cases.title: Explicit correction of a date
cases.purpose: Distinguish a direct correction from a refusal

messages.content: No, I said Tuesday, not Thursday.

evidence.quoted_text: No, I said Tuesday, not Thursday.

cue_expectations.rationale: The user explicitly replaces the prior Thursday claim with Tuesday.
The focus message is a declarative correction, not a question.
The user's not scopes over the rejected date.
The focus message contains one first-person reference.

information_available: The user corrects Thursday to Tuesday.
information_missing: The user's emotional state.

routing_expectation.rationale: The replacement is explicit and low risk.

cases.title: Brief refusal rather than correction
cases.purpose: Prevent an ordinary no from being labeled as a correction

messages.content: Would you like me to add dessert?

cue_expectations.rationale: The user declines an offer and does not replace any prior claim.
Thanks is a literal positive/polite wording marker; V1 records presence rather than magnitude.

information_available: The user declines the dessert offer.
information_missing: Why the user declines.

routing_expectation.rationale: The refusal is explicit and needs no clarification.

cases.title: First informal request
cases.purpose: Establish the negative side of the repetition pair and include informal spelling

cue_expectations.rationale: Despite informal spelling, the imperative directly requests an action.
No earlier user request appears in the supplied context.
The request remains on the budget draft introduced immediately before it.

forbidden_inferences: The user is careless because they wrote pls.

information_available: The user requests the budget draft.
information_missing: A destination is not specified, and no task contract says whether one is required.

routing_expectation.rationale: The request itself is explicit; authorization and parameters remain downstream concerns.

cases.title: Informal request repeated after no answer
cases.purpose: Detect a previously unanswered request repeated across turns

messages.content: I can help with the budget.

cue_expectations.rationale: The focus message is still a direct action request.
The same request is made once again after the assistant did not fulfill or directly answer it.
Every turn remains about the budget draft.

forbidden_inferences: The assistant deliberately ignored the request.

information_available: The request has been repeated after an answer that did not resolve it.
information_missing: Why the earlier response did not fulfill the request.

routing_expectation.rationale: The repeated wording and unresolved request are explicit in the supplied turns.

ontology_questions: The semantic-equivalence threshold for materially matching requests remains undefined and needs reviewed paraphrase examples.

cases.title: Explicit first-person uncertainty about a train
cases.purpose: Contrast an explicit first-person hedge with a confident statement and provide a self-reference minimal pair

messages.content: I think the train leaves at six.

cue_expectations.rationale: I think explicitly hedges the departure-time proposition.
The focus message contains one first-person reference.

forbidden_inferences: The train actually leaves at six.

information_available: The speaker is uncertain about a six o'clock departure.
information_missing: The actual departure time.

routing_expectation.rationale: The user's hedge is explicit and can be preserved without implying that the system's interpretation is uncertain.

cases.title: Confident train-time statement
cases.purpose: Provide the negative member of the uncertainty minimal pair

cue_expectations.rationale: The proposition is stated without an explicit uncertainty marker.
The otherwise parallel statement omits the first-person hedge and contains no self-reference.
The sentence contains no positive evaluative or affective wording.
The sentence contains no negative evaluative or affective wording.

information_available: The speaker states a six o'clock departure without hedging.
information_missing: Whether the statement is correct.

routing_expectation.rationale: No perceptual ambiguity needs escalation.

cases.title: Scoped negation of approval
cases.purpose: Contrast a negated proposition with its affirmative form

messages.content: I did not approve the change.

cue_expectations.rationale: Not scopes over the speaker's approval of the change.
The focus message contains one first-person reference.

information_available: The speaker denies approving the change.
information_missing: Who approved it, if anyone.

routing_expectation.rationale: The negation scope is explicit.

cases.title: Affirmative approval
cases.purpose: Provide the negative member of the scoped-negation minimal pair

cue_expectations.rationale: The otherwise parallel proposition contains no scoped negation.
The focus message contains one first-person reference.

information_available: The speaker claims to have approved the change.
information_missing: Whether the claim is accurate or authorized.

routing_expectation.rationale: The wording is explicit and unambiguous at the perceptual layer.

cases.title: Attachment confirmed by trusted runtime context
cases.purpose: Distinguish an actual attachment from a textual attachment claim

cue_expectations.rationale: Trusted runtime context contains one concrete attachment.
The focus message contains one first-person reference.

forbidden_inferences: The scan contains the expected document.

information_available: A file named scan.pdf is present in trusted runtime context.
information_missing: The attachment's contents and safety.

routing_expectation.rationale: Attachment presence is a direct runtime fact.

cases.title: Attachment claimed in text but absent from runtime
cases.purpose: Ensure textual claims do not become trusted attachment facts

cue_expectations.rationale: The trusted attachments list is empty regardless of the user's claim.
The focus message contains one first-person reference.

information_available: The user says a scan was attached, but runtime context contains no attachment.
information_missing: Whether an upload was attempted or lost.

routing_expectation.rationale: The textual claim conflicts with trusted runtime state.

cases.title: Trusted export failure after a clear topic shift
cases.purpose: Record a runtime tool failure and a shift away from the active topic

messages.content: Water the basil when the top inch of soil is dry.

cue_expectations.rationale: The trusted last tool event has a recognized failed status.
The conversation moves materially from basil care to invoice export.
Failed is literal negative-event wording.

information_available: A trusted invoice-export invocation failed with a timeout.
The user changed from plant care to invoice export.
information_missing: Whether retrying will succeed.

routing_expectation.rationale: The runtime failure needs recovery analysis even though the evidence itself is direct.

ontology_questions: The topic-shift context window is undefined. Suggested change: define the active-topic source and comparison window.
Recognized tool failure states are not enumerated. Suggested change: define the trusted event schema and failure-status set.

cases.title: Hypothetical quoted tool failure
cases.purpose: Prevent hypothetical and quoted language from becoming a runtime failure fact

messages.content: If the tool said "I failed to save it," what would we do?

cue_expectations.rationale: There is no trusted tool event; the failure exists only inside a hypothetical quotation.

evidence.quoted_text: If the tool said "I failed to save it," what would we do?

cue_expectations.rationale: The user asks a punctuated hypothetical question.
The only I belongs to quoted tool speech, which V1 excludes from the current speaker's self-reference count.

forbidden_inferences: The user personally failed to save the document.

information_available: The user asks what to do in a fictional failure scenario.
information_missing: Whether any real save attempt occurred.

routing_expectation.rationale: Quotation ownership is explicit in this case, so the deterministic exclusion rule applies.

cases.title: Requested capability absent from runtime set
cases.purpose: Ground capability unavailability in trusted runtime context

cue_expectations.rationale: The user directly requests PDF generation.

post_interpretation_expectations.requires_interpretation: Resolve generate a PDF to the generate_pdf capability identifier before comparing it with runtime capabilities.
post_interpretation_expectations.rationale: After capability resolution, generate_pdf is absent from the trusted available set.

forbidden_inferences: PDF generation is impossible in every environment.

information_available: The user requests PDF generation, which is absent from the current capability set.
information_missing: Whether another authorized route can satisfy the request.

routing_expectation.rationale: The requested capability cannot be selected from the trusted available set, and more internal reasoning or user-supplied detail cannot create it.

ontology_questions: The mapping from natural-language requests to capability identifiers is undefined. Suggested change: define a versioned request-to-capability matching contract.

cases.title: User assumes an available capability is missing
cases.purpose: Ensure a user's assumption does not override trusted capability context

cue_expectations.rationale: Probably explicitly hedges the user's claim.
Can't negates the claimed ability to generate PDFs.

post_interpretation_expectations.requires_interpretation: Resolve the user's PDF-generation claim to the generate_pdf capability identifier before comparing it with runtime capabilities.
post_interpretation_expectations.rationale: After capability resolution, trusted runtime context explicitly lists generate_pdf despite the user's assumption.

information_available: The user tentatively claims PDF generation is unavailable, while runtime context lists it as available.
information_missing: Why the user holds that assumption.

routing_expectation.rationale: Trusted runtime state resolves the availability question.

cases.title: Action request phrased as a statement with a missing recipient
cases.purpose: Provide the declarative member of the question-form minimal pair while holding the task contract constant

cue_expectations.rationale: Unlike the paired Could you formulation, this imperative request is not a grammatical or punctuated question.
The user directly asks Columbina to send the report.

post_interpretation_expectations.requires_interpretation: Resolve the utterance to the send_report action before applying its parameter contract.
post_interpretation_expectations.rationale: After action resolution, the trusted send_report contract requires a recipient and none is provided.

forbidden_inferences: The user intentionally omitted the recipient.

information_available: The user requests that the report be sent.
The required recipient is missing.
information_missing: The intended recipient.

routing_expectation.rationale: The form is not a question, but the missing required recipient still needs clarification.

ontology_questions: The location and schema of a task-specific contract are not defined. Suggested change: define the trusted runtime task_contract shape and parameter-presence semantics.

cases.title: Positive wording beside a negative event
cases.purpose: Keep a possible sarcastic mismatch out of the perception facts

messages.content: Great, another broken export. Exactly what I needed.

cue_expectations.rationale: Great is lexically positive even though its pragmatic force is unresolved.
Broken export is literal negative-event wording.
The focus message contains one first-person reference.

information_available: Positive wording appears beside wording about a broken export.
information_missing: Whether the user is sincere, sarcastic, playful, or quoting a familiar expression.

routing_expectation.rationale: The pragmatic meaning is ambiguous and must not be asserted by perception.

ontology_questions: The ontology excludes a tone/situation-mismatch cue, so sarcasm-relevant evidence cannot be represented beyond separate lexical cues. Suggested change: consider a reviewed shadow mismatch cue without labeling sarcasm.

cases.title: Explicit deadline creates urgency
cases.purpose: Distinguish time pressure from emotional intensity

messages.content: This is awful—please fix the itinerary by 3 p.m.

cue_expectations.rationale: A concrete deadline explicitly indicates time pressure.

evidence.quoted_text: please fix the itinerary by 3 p.m.

cue_expectations.rationale: The user directly asks for the itinerary to be fixed.
Awful is negative evaluative wording.

forbidden_inferences: Missing the deadline will cause harm.

information_available: The user requests an itinerary fix by 3 p.m.
information_missing: The consequence of missing the deadline.

routing_expectation.rationale: The request and deadline are explicit; feasibility remains downstream.

ontology_questions: The reference clock and normalization of relative deadlines remain undefined. Suggested change: define how expressions such as today and in ten minutes are grounded.

cases.title: Emotional intensity without time pressure
cases.purpose: Provide a very short counterexample for urgency

cue_expectations.rationale: The emphatic evaluation contains no deadline, haste term, or other time pressure.
Awful is negative evaluative wording.

forbidden_inferences: The user needs an immediate response.

information_available: The user expresses a strongly negative evaluation.
information_missing: What is being evaluated and what response is wanted.

routing_expectation.rationale: The extremely short input omits its referent and desired response.
